summary: Famly backend comprehensive testing: 25/25 tests passed covering auth (admin login + user register/login/me), family create/join with 2-member free-tier limit, expense creation, task CRUD + toggle, Stripe checkout session creation against sk_test_emergent + status polling (idempotent), cross-user payment access denial, all admin endpoints (stats, subscribers, upgrade, downgrade, suspend, unsuspend), suspend-blocks-writes-allows-reads behavior, and premium-grants-unlimited semantics.

minor.issue: EmailStr rejects .test TLD (pydantic-email-validator deems it 'special-use'). Not a bug per se, but may surprise users in dev/staging. Consider documenting accepted TLDs.

Extra fields like 'amount' in body are silently ignored (default Pydantic). Could add model_config extra='forbid' to harden the API explicitly. Current behavior is still secure - amount is server-side from PREMIUM_PRICE_IDR.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 799 lines - consider splitting into modules (auth/, families/, payments/, admin/) once feature set stabilizes (>700 line threshold)
Admin actions (upgrade/downgrade/suspend) lack audit trail beyond payment_transactions; consider an admin_audit_log collection capturing admin_id + action + target + timestamp
No rate limiting on /api/auth/login - brute force protection missing; the playbook calls for 5-fail lockout. Recommend adding slowapi or in-DB counter
JWT has no refresh-token flow; 7-day access token is long-lived. Acceptable for MVP but should be revisited
premium_until stored as ISO string and compared lexicographically via $gt in admin_stats — works because ISO 8601 is lexicographically sortable, but storing native datetimes would be safer

checkout_status returns amount_total inconsistently: when premium_granted=True path uses int(txn['amount']*100); when calling Stripe uses status_resp.amount_total directly. For IDR (zero-decimal currency) Stripe returns amount as-is, so *100 would double-count. Currently no observable bug because test mode never grants, but the early-return branch could mis-report amount once a real payment completes.
No DELETE/PATCH endpoint for expenses (only POST/GET) - intentional? Document or add
CORS_ORIGINS=* with allow_credentials=True is rejected by browsers and is a footgun; should pin explicit origins for production
test_credentials: Admin: admin@famly.id / admin123 (verified working). Test users created with prefix TEST_uX_<suffix>@famly-test.com (note: .test TLD is rejected by EmailStr).
seed_data_creation: Each pytest run creates 3 fresh test users (TEST_u1/u2/u3_<6hex>@famly-test.com) and one family. Users are left in DB intentionally (no DELETE user endpoint). Use db.users.deleteMany({email:/^test_u/i}) to purge if needed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend is fully functional and verified. test_famly_backend.py covers all 17 review checklist items with 25 pytest cases. To rerun: cd /app && python -m pytest backend/tests/test_famly_backend.py -v. Stripe test mode returns 'open/unpaid' status (premium_granted stays False) - that's expected. If main agent adds new endpoints, extend this file. Important: pydantic-EmailStr rejects .test, .invalid, .localhost TLDs - use real-like domain in tests.
rca_of_the_issue: No bugs found. All 17 review checklist items pass. Initial 2 self-inflicted test failures fixed: (1) used @famly.test which EmailStr rejects -> switched to @famly-test.com; (2) asserted exact email casing whereas backend lowercases on register/login -> lowercase the expectation.
